articles.title: Netflix Orders Lonesome Dove TV Series From East of Eden Showrunners
articles.summary: Netflix has ordered a series retelling of Larry McMurtry's Pulitzer Prize-winning Western novel Lonesome Dove. The project will reteam the streaming service with East of Eden co-showrunners Zoe Kazan and Jeb Stuart.
body: McMurtry's 1985 bestseller follows former Texas Rangers-turned-cowboys Augustus "Gus" McRae and Woodrow Call, who embark on a fateful 3000-mile cattle drive to Montana, encountering a variety of frontier dangers along the way.

CBS adapted it as a blockbuster TV miniseries in 1989 starring Robert Duvall, Tommy Lee Jones, Danny Glover, Rick Schroder, Diane Lane, Robert Urich, Anjelica Huston, Steve Buscemi, Chris Cooper, Frederic Forrest, and Glenne Headly.

“After our singular experience on East of Eden, we are thrilled to be teaming with Netflix again, along with Teton Ridge Entertainment, to bring Larry McMurtry’s western classic to life,” Kazan and Stuart said in a statement (via Deadline ).
“We come to this material with love and respect, and can’t wait to hit the trail with Gus and Call and the rest of these beloved characters. Yee-haw.”
points: Netflix has ordered a series retelling of Larry McMurtry's Pulitzer Prize-winning Western novel Lonesome Dove.
The project will reteam the streaming service with East of Eden co-showrunners Zoe Kazan and Jeb Stuart.

articles.title: 'Battlestar Galactica' Meets 'Hunger Games' in 100-Episode Action Thriller That's Free on Streaming
articles.summary: Battlestar Galactica and The Hunger Games thrive on a similar kind of pressure. Both trap remnants of human civilization within unforgiving systems with brutally high stakes where one slip-up means certain death.
body: That same volatile combination powers The 100, The CW’s post-apocalyptic action series that premiered in 2014 and ran for exactly 100 episodes. All 100 of those episodes are currently free to stream on Pluto TV.

Set 97 years after a nuclear catastrophe rendered Earth uninhabitable, the series follows the descendants of humanity’s survivors aboard the Ark, an orbital space station with a rapidly failing life-support system. Their potential solution is as absurd as it is delicious: Send 100 beautiful, incarcerated teenagers to the ruins of Earth to see whether radiation burns them alive from the inside out.

The titular 100 are a motley assortment of petty criminals, violent offenders, and Clarke Griffin (Eliza Taylor), a political prisoner locked up after discovering that the Ark is running out of oxygen. There’s also Octavia Blake (Marie Avgeropoulos), who was imprisoned for the unforgivable offense of being born (people can’t have more than one child). Once the 100 reach the ground, however, they discover a fresh start in a beautiful, dangerous world where nobody is coming to enforce the rules — and humanity may not be quite as extinct as they were told.
points: Battlestar Galactica and The Hunger Games thrive on a similar kind of pressure.
Both trap remnants of human civilization within unforgiving systems with brutally high stakes where one slip-up means certain death.

articles.title: Marvel Phase 7 and 8 Movie Slate and Release Dates: 'Black Panther 3,' 'Shang-Chi 2' and Beyond
articles.summary: Like Doctor Strange himself, Marvel Studios has its eyes fixed on the future, with a carefully plotted release calendar extending well beyond the highly anticipated events of Avengers: Secret Wars, which is currently set to hit theaters in December 2027.
body: Marvel’s release calendar is always subject to change, but the studio’s plans after Secret Wars are becoming easier to read. The MCU’s next era seemingly won’t be built around the same heroes who carried the Infinity Saga, as the X-Men and Marvel’s supernatural characters appear poised to steal the limelight.

Based on Marvel’s announced projects, Kevin Feige’s comments, and the studio’s current direction, here’s what Phase 7 might look like. Keep in mind that although Marvel has booked these release dates, its two 2029 movies remain entirely speculative.

In the wake of Doomsday, Marvel’s Secret Wars will drop its heroes into one of their most harrowing situations yet. Although little has been confirmed about the movie’s plot, its title evokes two landmark comic-book crossovers. The original 1984 story brought Marvel’s heroes and villains together on a patchwork planet created by the Beyonder, while Jonathan Hickman and Esad Ribić’s 2015 series followed Doctor Doom as he ruled a new Battleworld assembled from the remains of destroyed realities.

articles.title: SteelSeries Aeon Pro Review So Far
articles.summary: The SteelSeries Aeon Pro is one of the most advanced controllers I've ever tested. It's also the most expensive – but it brings some features never before seen in a controller.
body: Notably, the Aeon Pro borrows the outstanding "infinite battery" system from the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro line of gaming headsets. Instead of relying on a cable or dock to charge the controller, the Aeon Pro has two rechargeable batteries – one in the controller and another that charges in the base station. Like the Nova Pro, when one battery runs out of juice, you simply pop it out and swap it with the fully-charged one from the base station. In less than 10 seconds, your controller is fully juiced up and the previously depleted battery is tucked back in the dock to charge.

I'm a big believer in this "infinite" battery system. It's one of the most revolutionary features to come to gaming headsets and is the reason I continue to recommend the Arctis Nova Pro, so I'm thrilled to see SteelSeries implement it in a controller. Even better, the base station also serves as a dock for the controller, giving it a home to live on your desk or entertainment center when not in use.
points: The SteelSeries Aeon Pro is one of the most advanced controllers I've ever tested.
It's also the most expensive – but it brings some features never before seen in a controller.

articles.title: Forget 'GTA 6,' The Greatest Miami Action Crime Series Ever Made Is Streaming For Free Right Now
articles.summary: Some shows change television forever. Anthologies have never been the same since The Twilight Zone, the modern sitcom owes a lot to I Love Lucy, and puzzle-box mysteries all had to step up their game after Lost.
body: Speaking of crime dramas with unforgettable legacies, Miami Vice (1984–1990) also left a massive cultural imprint. Although the NBC show did nothing novel in terms of storytelling, Miami Vice ’s use of striking pastel shades and frenetic camera work made it stand out from genre fare. If you’ve been meaning to check this groundbreaking series out, there’s good news: All five seasons of Miami Vice are now available to stream for free on Tubi.

Miami Vice follows detective sergeants James "Sonny" Crockett (Don Johnson) and Ricardo "Rico" Tubbs (Philip Michael Thomas), who team up to fight crime — and do so in style. Crockett and Tubbs are supported by a core cast and a revolving door of guest stars, including the likes of Laurence Fishburne, Viggo Mortensen, Ben Stiller, Bruce Willis, and Liam Neeson, among others. Following a case-of-the-week format, Miami Vice keeps things fairly lighthearted in the initial seasons, but turns darker and more cynical as Crockett and Tubbs explore the seedy underbelly of crime and corruption in the neon-tinted streets of Miami.

articles.title: Xbox Game Pass Adds A Great Call Of Duty Game Today
articles.summary: Xbox Game Pass grows today with the addition of a popular Call of Duty game. New to the service from today, September 8, is 2020's Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War. It's available on Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, and PC Game Pass, and the game supports cloud streaming as well.
body: Developed by Treyarch and Raven, Black Ops Cold War is set in Cold War-era 1981, with its campaign following Russell Adler as he and his team seek out a spy named Perseus. The game also has multiplayer, of course, along with Zombies.
Black Ops Cold War was a bit hit, becoming 2020's best-selling game overall in the US.
Game Pass isn't done adding more titles this month, as The Royal Writ and Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O World Stage arrive on September 10, followed by RuneScape: Dragonwilds on September 15.

After Microsoft bought Activision Blizzard, many assumed that back-catalog Call of Duty games would flood Game Pass, but that didn't happen. Instead of releasing Call of Duty games en masse to Game Pass, Microsoft has taken more of a selective approach. Black Ops Cold War is now just the sixth Call of Duty game on Game Pass, joining Call of Duty: WWII, Call of Duty: Vanguard, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, and Black Ops 6.

articles.title: Steam may have leaked achievements for countless forthcoming PC games via a third party site, including Persona 6, Ace Combat 8, and even some unannounced games
articles.summary: Exophase, a site dedicated to tracking achievements for games across all major platforms including Steam, appears to have been flooded with a bunch of achievements lists it really shouldn't have yet.
body: Among those, possibly the biggest surprise is Persona 6. It doesn't even have a release window yet, but its achievements list —assuming it's as legitimate as it looks—is rife with plausible spoilers. You have been warned: there is a lot in there, considering Atlus hasn't even shown gameplay footage yet.

Meanwhile, the achievements list for Kingdom Hearts 4 may reveal a lot about the 2027 instalment that Square Enix no doubt wants to keep under wraps. For example (huge spoilers ahead), Reddit fans have gleaned from the achievements which worlds from Disney's extended universe are most likely to appear, including the corroboration of a widely-believed rumor. Again, you've been warned.

The torrent of listings even includes Steam games that haven't been announced or named in Steam's backend yet. Among the more interesting examples are a possible Balatro follow-up (update: it's not a real one) and seemingly verified rumors that the forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered will come with a new campaign called The Tarnished Mirror.
It also looks like Squadron 42, the singleplayer campaign component of Star Citizen which was delayed to Q2 2027 last week, may make its way to Steam.

articles.title: Xbox’s Disc-To-Digital Program Has A Big Problem: Several Major Publishers Aren’t Participating
articles.summary: Xbox's disc-to-digital program looks like it could be a vital step forward for players who want to hold on to their physical games in an increasingly digital world, but it does have limits.
body: So far, it looks like games from Sega, Square Enix, Ubisoft, and Bandai Namco are largely incompatible with the disc-to-digital service. As verified by Kotaku, popping in a disc for a game from one of those publishers could result in a "not participating in digital licensing" message. A fan effort to catalogue all the games that do work with it also shows which titles from those publishers are incompatible with disc-to-digital, so if you were holding on to a physical edition of Far Cry 4, Final Fantasy 15, or Dark Souls 3, you're out of luck.

This is something that Square Enix has been called to task over, as several of its big HD-2D RPGs have no upgrade path to Switch 2. For example, if you purchased Octopath Traveler for the Switch, there's no complimentary or premium upgrade pack to give it sharper graphics and new features on a Switch 2 console. Instead, you'll have to buy the game again when its Switch 2 version launches, and you don't even get an option to transfer your save game over.
points: Xbox's disc-to-digital program looks like it could be a vital step forward for players who want to hold on to their physical games in an increasingly digital world, but it does have limits.

articles.title: Corporations want to kill physical media because it suits them, but Big Box PC game packaging just got a second chance
articles.summary: If you were alive and sentient in the nineties you probably harbour some fondness for the "big box" PC games of yore. Back then, rather than buy an ephemeral digital license for a game, you'd head to a store to buy a huge box bedecked in lavish art, inside which you'd find a handful of 3.5-inch…
body: There's been renewed interest in the ye olde big box PC game, especially in the wake of Sony's announcement it will discontinue physical PlayStation games. Some proactive folk have gone viral for manufacturing their own physical Steam games. Now GOG has offered its own alternative: printable big boxes based on scans of real commercial packages from the golden era of game packaging.

In collaboration with Big Box Collection—which is a fan-operated trove of big box 3D scans—GOG is now offering those 3D scans with five entries in its GOG Preservation Program. These include the newly added Star Trek: 25th Anniversary and Armikrog, while games already in the Preservation Program including Descent, Hitman: Codename 47, and Myst will also receive the treatment.

"We’re delivering flat, printable versions of the same box art, so you can cut, fold, and glue your own physical big box at home," reads GOG's announcement. "A proper papercraft project for anyone who misses shelves full of PC game boxes."

Players can get the rundown on the ongoings of Los Santos during the two years they've been gone.
points: Take a look at the Lore Trailer for nopixel V, the hit role-playing experience within Grand Theft Auto Online and GTA 5, developed by nopixel Studios in collaboration with Rockstar Games.
